Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The CNIe v2 supports digital authentication via NFC, PIN, face biometrics, and fingerprint. The national digital ID platform (identitenumerique.ma) and Mon identite numerique mobile app enable remote digital authentication. The platform supports multi-factor authentication (MFA). As of September 2025, over 7 million digital identity transactions have been processed since April 2022.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: The national digital ID platform enables authentication for government e-services. Morocco had 600 public services online by 2024. The Idarati X.0 (2026) is designed as a unified entry point for digital public services authenticated by the CNIe. DGSN E-Police portal uses digital ID. Ministries of Justice, Habitat, Youth, CNSS, and tax authority (DGI) have all adopted the Mon e-ID app for government portal authentication.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Citizens can access and manage their digital identity data through the identitenumerique.ma portal and Mon identite numerique app. Citizens can: activate/deactivate digital identity, manage authentication factors, track history of authentication transactions, and view/modify consent. Law 09-08 grants individuals the right to access and rectify their personal data.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: The CNIe chip embeds ICAO and eID applications for eKYC. The IDEMIA case study explicitly describes the system enabling eKYC for banks, insurance companies and digital signature services. KYC compliance in Morocco requires the CIN as primary identity document. Banks have integrated Mon e-ID for KYC within 48 hours. BAM Directive 5/W/2017 governs KYC due diligence using national ID.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: General judicial oversight applies via Morocco's court system and CNDP enforcement mechanisms. Courts handle identity disputes and the CNIE law (35-06) was promulgated through the Royal Decree. The CNDP can refer data protection violations to the public prosecutor. No specific dedicated ID oversight tribunal identified. The DGSN's forensic laboratory holds ISO 17025 certification and courts are integrated into digital ID use (Ministry of Justice connected to Trusted Third Party Platform in 2024).

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Civil registration (managed by DGCL) is a prerequisite for CNIE enrollment - a birth certificate is required to apply. However, the World Bank ID4D diagnostic (2018) noted the link is largely paper-based rather than electronic; CNIE checks birth registration act as a documentary prerequisite. The MOSIP-based Registre National des Populations (for social protection) is linked to civil registry data. Full electronic interoperability between CRVS and ID registry is not yet established; UNFPA 2022 Arab CRVS assessment noted coordination gaps in Morocco.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Law 09-08 requires CNDP authorization for data sharing and interconnections. The digital ID platform uses a 'Trusted Third Party' model where citizen data is not stored by service providers. The Digital X.0 draft law (2025) introduces a traceable consent mechanism for data exchanges between institutions. Some rules exist but comprehensive publicly-available data sharing framework for the ID system is still being developed.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Morocco has digital ID-specific legislation. Law No. 35-06 (Dahir 1-07-149, 2007) established the CNIE system. The 2020 decree specifically governs the new-generation CNIE mandating it for citizens 16+. The Trusted Third Party Platform for Digital Identity Authentication operates under a specific regulatory framework. The Digital X.0 draft law (2025) further addresses digital identity.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 09-08 on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data was adopted on 18 February 2009. It governs collection, use, storage and transfer of personal data including biometric data. Enforced by the CNDP. Applies to all data controllers including identity system operators.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Commission Nationale de controle de la Protection des Donnees Personnelles (CNDP) was established by Law 09-08 (2009). It is an independent supervisory authority with powers to investigate, sanction, and oversee all personal data processing including the national ID system. The CNDP co-signed the 2023 agreement for digital ID use in health services, confirming its active oversight role.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The CNIE is the legally recognized proof of identity, nationality, and residence in Morocco. It replaces the birth certificate, certificate of residence, proof of life, and certification of nationality. Required by law for all citizens aged 16+. Used as legal proof in all administrative, banking, judicial and commercial transactions.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: The CNIE system is instituted by Law No. 35-06 promulgated by Dahir (Royal Decree No. 1-07-149 of 30 November 2007) and executive order (Decree No. 2-06-478 of 25 December 2007). The new-generation CNIe was governed by decree examined by the Council of Government in 2020 mandating CNIE for all citizens aged 16+. Law 09-08 (2009) governs data protection. The Digital X.0 draft law (2025) addresses digital identity governance.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: System delivered and maintained under contract with foreign vendor IDEMIA (French company), which provides engineering support, training, and hardware/software personalization systems at two DGSN personalization sites. The platform software is provided by iDAKTO (IDCluster). DGSN operates the system but relies on IDEMIA for engineering and maintenance. Partial in-country capacity through DGSN technical staff but foreign vendor dominates core maintenance.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The CNIE program is primarily operated by DGSN under the Ministry of Interior, not the Ministry of Finance. However, the World Bank DPF program (2020, EUR 459.8 million) was implemented through the Ministry of Economy and Finance, indicating some finance ministry involvement in digital inclusion programs. The Idarati X.0 project involves multi-ministry coordination. Ministry of Finance oversight of the ID system specifically is partial rather than full.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The CNIE system is primarily funded by the domestic government (DGSN/Ministry of Interior budget). The new-generation CNIe and digital platform were developed under a government-contracted partnership with IDEMIA (2019 strategic contract). The Registre National des Populations is World Bank-financed. Overall financing is mixed - core CNIE operations are domestic while digital transformation initiatives include World Bank DPF (USD 500 million, 2020) and international vendor contracts.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The CNIE system collects both fingerprints (10-finger AFIS) and facial biometrics. The IDEMIA-supplied CNIe v2 (from 2020) stores face and fingerprint templates on the contactless chip. The digital platform supports face and fingerprint authentication including liveness detection. Iris not collected.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The National Identity Registry is a fully digital database. CNIE system implemented since 2008 with a central digital back-end managed by DGSN. The system uses an Automated Fingerprint Identification System (AFIS) for deduplication. All enrollment data and biometric templates are stored digitally.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Morocco's CNIE (Carte Nationale d'Identite Electronique) is fully deployed nationwide. The new-generation CNIe system launched in August 2020 via DGSN-IDEMIA partnership. National digital ID platform (identitenumerique.ma) launched May 2022. About 20 million active CNI cards issued covering ~85% of population. DGSN issued 4.6 million digital IDs in 2024 alone.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The IDEMIA-delivered system implements the OSIA standard for interoperability and iDAKTO's IDCluster platform. 30+ public and private institutions connected to the Trusted Third Party Identity Verification platform by 2024. The Idarati X.0 initiative (2026) is explicitly built on system interoperability among government agencies. Digital X.0 draft law also mandates interoperability.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The CNIE is mandatory for opening a bank account in Morocco (ID4D diagnostic confirmed). Bank Al-Maghrib framework agreements were signed in 2024 with DGSN for digital ID use. KYC regulations require the CIN as the primary identification document for financial services. Banks have integrated Mon e-ID. The CNIE is used in nearly every aspect of transactional life including banking.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The CNIE is not free - a stamp duty (fee) of 75 MAD is charged for applicants over age 12, and 50 MAD for applicants under age 12. The credential requires payment. Note: registration within 30 days of birth for civil registration is free, but the ID card itself carries a fee.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: The CNIe is ICAO DOC9303 compliant and Morocco has bilateral agreements. The DGSN established 71 centers at diplomatic missions processing 219,408 IDs for Moroccan expatriates in 2024. Morocco's CNIE is accepted in some regional contexts. No formal interoperability agreement with specific regional body (AU, Arab League) found for digital ID specifically. Some regional recognition exists through bilateral agreements.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The CNIE is mandatory for citizens aged 16+. Minors aged 12-15 may obtain a CNIE when applying for a passport. Children under 12 may also obtain one at request of a legal guardian (fee of 50 MAD). The 2020 decree specifies mandatory enrollment at 16, but eligibility starts earlier (can be obtained at any age). Primary mandatory threshold is 16 years (falls in the >17 category for mandatory, but is eligible from younger).

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Enrollment is mandatory for all Moroccan citizens aged 16 and over under the 2020 decree. Article 2 of the law stipulates 'any citizen aged 16 must have a national electronic identity card.' Non-compliance carries fines of 300-400 MAD. This applies to all citizens.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: In June 2023, the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, CNDP and DGSN signed an agreement allowing hospitals to verify patient identity through the digital ID scheme. Citizens can include health data (patient number, social protection number) on the CNIe chip. ID card is required for admission to secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities. Mon e-ID app adopted by health institutions. Mandatory status not confirmed for all health contexts.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Wikipedia reports ~20 million active CNI cards covering approximately 85% of the Moroccan population (total population ~37 million). DGSN issued 4.6 million digital IDs in 2024 alone. Earlier World Bank (2018) estimated ~60% of total population covered (75-80% of adult population 18+). Current coverage is estimated at 70-89% based on 85% figure cited by Wikipedia for all CNI types.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: The DGSN Scientific and Technical Police Laboratory holds ISO 17025 certification (2024). The CNIe system uses state-of-the-art security features including cryptographic credentials, NFC, ICAO compliance, and advanced encryption. Following cyberattacks on CNSS and Ministry of Justice in 2025, Morocco reviewed and reinforced its digital ID platform security. IDEMIA's solution meets international security standards. CNDP conducts oversight audits on data processing.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration in Morocco is mandatory by law since 2016. Every SIM must be linked to a valid identity document (CIN for Moroccan citizens, passport for foreigners) and activated via biometric verification at a physical point of sale. Operators must maintain a subscriber registry. Activating a SIM without identity verification violates current regulations.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The CNIE is required for access to social services. The World Bank-financed Registre National des Populations (10 million users by 2023) is linked to the CNIE system for social benefits management. DGSN 2024 report confirms digital ID integration with National Social Security Fund (CNSS). The CNIE serves as proof of life and residence for social services.
